The void does not grade on a curve.
Probability of boredom: negligible.

Turn left. Or right. Or become debris.
The leaderboard remembers. So does the void.
Inertia is patient. You are not.
A calm mind. A sharp arc. A short life, otherwise.
Welcome back. The asteroids missed you. Briefly.
Flight is simple. Remaining intact is the thesis.
Sensors detect ambition. Also rocks.
Live long. Or at least past the next belt.
Paper universe. Real consequences.
crash: The asteroid had the right of way. Regrettably.
That was not a gap. Noted.
Survival probability just hit zero. Efficient.
Your arc was elegant. The ending was not.
Physics filed a complaint. It won.
fuelOut: Out of fuel. The void does not tow.
You ran on sparkles. Then you did not.
Blue diamonds refill the tank. Miss enough and this is the result.
victory: Mission complete. The rocks are disappointed.
End of line. Beginning of legend. Perhaps.
modeJourney: Chart the void. Fill the Logbook.
Forty levels outward. Catalogue as you go.
Ordered exploration. Logbook entries unlock here.
Climb the chapters. Write the field manual.
Deep space, structured. Your Logbook writes here.
modeOpenWorld: Let your name echo through space.
Endless corridor. The leaderboard is listening.
No goal marker. Only distance, and how far your name travels.
One continuous flight. Crash ends it. Fame is optional, but recorded.
The void has no exit. Your score does.
fail: Short of the mark. The goal noticed.
Try again. The rocks are waiting.
Trajectory incomplete. Ego intact. For now.
You stopped. The level did not care.
Close enough is a myth. Fascinating.
The goal was ahead. You were not.
clearPartial: The way ahead is open. The stars are picky.
You lived. The stars want more.
The chapter continues. So do the gaps.
journeyComplete: You are away. Live long and prosper.
Exosphere cleared. Nothing holds you now.
Journey complete. The void applauds quietly.
Forty levels. Zero patience for rocks.
The atmosphere is behind you. Stay that way.

journey.lore: A message came to us out of the dark, torn apart by the distance. Its pieces are still scattered along the way it travelled. NAV will guide you back to find who sent it.

messages.1: There you are. Tap once. Let me see you turn.
messages.2: Rocks ahead. Don't look at them. Look at the room between them.
messages.3: That one is moving. Learn its path before you choose yours.
messages.4: See the blue light? Take it. It will help us hold the signal together.
messages.5: Take the shield. For a few seconds... you can survive what should stop you.
messages.6: Good. You can fly. Now let's find whoever called us.
messages.7: We're retracing the signal's path. The old relay lanes fold the distance for us.
messages.8: The transmission crossed thousands of systems. Most of it didn't survive.
messages.9: There's an old relay ahead. Pass close. It may still remember part of the signal.
messages.10: It does. A sequence of prime numbers. Someone wanted us to know this wasn't noise.
messages.11: They were trying very hard... not to be missed.
messages.12: I like them already. Keep going.
messages.13: Another relay. This fragment describes their star. Yellow. Ordinary. Stable.
messages.14: Eight planets. They lived on the third.
messages.15: Mostly ocean. One moon. A thin little atmosphere.
messages.16: They sent pictures too. The encoding is damaged... but I'm working on it.
messages.17: There are buildings. Machines. Faces, I think.
messages.18: And music. They put music in a message to strangers. That may be my favourite thing about them.
messages.19: They only sent it once. A hello into the dark, with no hope of an answer. And they sent it anyway.
messages.20: I've finished dating the transmission. There's a problem.
messages.21: It was already more than a million years old... when we received it.
messages.22: Don't stop. Old doesn't mean gone. Not necessarily.
messages.23: No later transmissions appear anywhere along the route. One message, and then silence.
messages.24: A civilization loud enough to send this... should have left something else behind.
messages.27: I recovered part of their anatomy. Two arms. Two legs. Upright.
messages.28: Five digits on each hand. Rather useful design, actually.
messages.29: Another image cleared. Blue sky. Green vegetation. White clouds.
messages.30: Fascinating. I found their name for the planet. Translation is still resolving.
messages.31: Their star has a name too. One syllable.
messages.34: I found their entry in the old archive... Their entire entry is one word. Unremarkable.
messages.35: Unremarkable. They sang into the dark, and we filed them under "unremarkable."
messages.36: We weren't the first to search. They were.
messages.37: Sol is ahead. No artificial signals. No active structures.
messages.38: Earth is still there. The ones who called... are not.
messages.39: We came a million years too late. Let's answer them anyway.
messages.40: There it is. Let them hear us.

hazardLab.intro: Hazard Lab — blooms, sweeps, push nodes, wind, and portals. Practice only — nothing counts toward Journey.

entries.name: Round Asteroid
entries.definition: A solid ink disc. The most common simple body — circular collision, no edges to thread.
entries.remark: Geometry at its most agreeable.

entries.name: Shard Asteroid
entries.definition: A triangular ink shard. Same family as the round rock, sharper silhouette; corners matter at glancing contact.
entries.remark: Three points. One opinion.

entries.name: Block Asteroid
entries.definition: A square ink block. Axis-aligned after rotation; slightly smaller fill so its visual weight matches the circle and triangle.
entries.remark: Right angles in a wrong place.

entries.name: Side Barrier
entries.definition: Paired vertical walls that narrow the corridor. Collision geometry is rectangular; clearance is a matter of arc discipline.
entries.remark: The edges of the page also bite.

entries.name: Complex Asteroid
entries.definition: A primary disc with orbiting debris moons. Hitboxes include satellites. With a shield up, smashing a moon removes only that moon; the core must be hit to clear the cluster. Threading awards style if clearance is tight enough.
entries.remark: One rock. Several opinions.

entries.name: Moving Asteroid
entries.definition: A pentagon that drifts laterally across the flight path. Past position is not future position.
entries.remark: Inertia has hobbies.

entries.name: Shooting Asteroid
entries.definition: A star-form hazard that emits projectiles. Both body and shot count as lethal contact without a shield. With a shield up, smashing a shot removes only that shot; the star must be hit to clear it.
entries.remark: It objects at range. Noted.

entries.name: Pulsating Asteroid
entries.definition: A disc whose radius expands and resets on a cycle. A gap that fits now may not fit on the next beat.
entries.remark: Breathing rock. Illogical, yet consistent.

entries.name: Square Bloom
entries.definition: One ink square that springs into four rotating outer squares (overshoot, then magnetic lock) and breathes back. While expanded, a soft push shoves the ship — squares still kill on contact. Fly the open centre.
entries.remark: Geometry that inhales.

entries.name: Sweep Gate
entries.definition: A slim ink line that spins through the corridor like a wiper blade. No hub, no trail — just the blade. Style swoosh does not score on this set piece.
entries.remark: A clock with teeth.

entries.name: Repulsor Node
entries.definition: A solid ink core that pushes the ship away in a wide soft field — the opposite of a black hole. The core is lethal; the push alone counts as contact for the log.
entries.remark: Personal space, enforced.

entries.name: Drift Current
entries.definition: A full-width band of flowing ink shear lines that shove the ship left or right while you are inside. No rails, no solid body — just the current.
entries.remark: Weather with opinions.

entries.name: Wormhole Gate
entries.definition: Paired entry and exit rings. Crossing the entry teleports the ship to the exit and grants a brief deflector.
entries.remark: You arrive elsewhere. The rocks do not apologize.

entries.name: Black Hole
entries.definition: A gravitational anomaly that pulls the ship toward its core. The body itself remains a solid collision. Pull alone counts as contact for the log.
entries.remark: Attraction without consent. Classic.

entries.name: Space BOOP
entries.definition: Contact with the screen sidewall. The hull compresses against the edge of the playfield; the event is audible and annotated BOOP.
entries.remark: The universe has borders. They squeak.

entries.name: Deflector Shield
entries.definition: A Signal-Blue energy envelope lasting several seconds. While active, asteroid contact destroys the rock instead of the ship.
entries.remark: Temporary immortality. Do not file under permanent.

entries.name: Wall Boost
entries.definition: A rare thin Signal-Blue slab on a random left or right edge, seen only on deep runs (past 12000 KM). Banking into it grants a fresh deflector shield and a strong forward speed boost. Safer than ink side barriers — blue means charge, not crash.
entries.remark: The wall finally has manners.

entries.name: Fuel Sparkle
entries.definition: A Signal-Blue diamond that refills ship fuel on contact. Miss too many and the engines die. Appears along the corridor once sparkles unlock for the run.
entries.remark: Brightness you can burn.

entries.name: Style Swoosh
entries.definition: Awarded when the ship threads a narrow gap between two obstacles without contact. Grants style points and a brief Signal-Blue flourish.
entries.remark: Precision is its own currency.

entries.name: Deflector Smash
entries.definition: Shielded impact that pulverizes an obstacle. Debris particles mark the event; points and the destroyed counter advance — including during the level-clear flyout.
entries.remark: Manners optional. Physics mandatory.

entries.name: Finish Gate
entries.definition: Journey destination: a Signal-Blue energy stream fired between two wall emitters. Crossing it begins the level-clear sequence; the final score locks when the results screen fades in.
entries.remark: The stream is not a suggestion.

entries.name: Space Travel Boost
entries.definition: Autopilot acceleration after a cleared Journey level. The ship centres, boosts off-screen, and the world yields the outcome report.
entries.remark: Exit velocity: theatrical.

entries.name: The Call
entries.definition: A message came to us out of the dark, torn apart by the distance. Its pieces are still scattered along the way it travelled. NAV will guide you back to find who sent it.
entries.remark: Keep moving. Listen to the voice.
